data.design: The existing glass bottle is wrapped in an old sleeve; Mother shows its measure while teaching the child. Preserve that ordinary hand-carried shape. Proposed returnable versions use plain glass and a simple stopper. No occult seal, glowing contents or rarity aura.

description:
Ordinary lamp fuel connects the oil seller’s shop, the working harbour and the lighthouse’s great upstairs lamp. In the household errand, Mother’s bottle is already paid for; the seller hands it over after the shop is unlocked. Measuring it, trimming the wick and turning the brass wheel make keeping a light a learned task. The oil does not explain the lower lamp or establish a ritual ingredient.

Proposed recurring use: recognizable returnable bottles make a short delivery visible on the seller’s rack. A stolen marked load can later connect an everyday shortage to a particular dock buyer. A bottle offered in thanks remains useful fuel, not a magical upgrade.

data.description: Established ordinary coastal cargo. A specific shop resupply network is proposed.
Used in the great upstairs lamp during Mother’s lesson.
Existing opening handover after the keys are returned and the seller opens the shop.

data.sections: §§5.2, 8.1 and 30: oil errand, proposed criminal fuel control and ordinary dock cargo; returnable-bottle design is new.

name: Lamp oil
